cells.tense: You are holding the fair read of a room while it is still happening.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Pick a custom the group has carried a while, and name which part still does real work. Drop the rest where they can see the going.
cells.core:
When a group's feeling runs high, you can stand in the middle of it and still tell what's fair. That's what's operating here: you feel what's happening without getting swept. The moves most people make — take sides fast, or go quiet to stay safe — aren't how you work.
Where this is going well, you keep a practice alive because it still carries something for the people in it. Right now some of what you're holding is being held past its use. You keep it going because stopping feels like losing something, when stopping is what would protect the part actually worth keeping. Name the part that has finished, drop it in the open, and stay while it settles.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what's fair while the feeling is still moving.
cells.verb: Governing what everyone feels with a fair hand
cells.place: In the shared ground where meaning is passed from person to person

cells.tense: You are going to be torn between two people before it has even begun.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Choose one disagreement inside the shared thing you care about. Carry both positions for a single conversation without deciding who's right — steady, and slow to move.
cells.core:
You read emotion fast, so when a group is about to split, you get there ahead of them — with a plan, a fairness already worked out, the whole settlement drafted before a word is spoken. You'll have decided who was out of line before the meeting starts. It looks like being fair. It's more like being the only judge in a case nobody filed.
Fairness doesn't need you computing it in advance. What's fair is what's left when you stop ruling and let two people stand where you can see both. Take the disagreement that's coming, and carry both positions in your hands without settling either. You're strong enough to hold both for one conversation. That's what the strength is for.
cells.sheetLine: You're writing the verdict before anyone has spoken.
cells.verb: Governing what everyone feels with a fair hand
cells.place: In the shared ground where meaning is passed from person to person

cells.tense: You stood at the door of something shared and did not quite go in.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Take something passed down that you've kept at arm's length, and put its actual events on paper in order — what happened, when, who was there — with no feeling words.
cells.core:
There's a tradition that shaped you, or a group whose meaning you were meant to share, and you did not fully arrive in it. You know it well enough to talk about it from outside. You're not standing in it.
Throwing yourself in and feeling it harder won't do it. Begin with what you can see. Take that thing handed down to you and put its actual events on paper, in order — what happened, when, who was there — with none of your feelings about it in the notes. That isn't avoidance. It's how something becomes a fact you can look at, and then, later, yours again. A clear fact is a doorway. Set one on the page and stand there a while.

cells.tense: You are holding a group's fairness steady and calling it just how things are.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Where a group is settling what something means, hear one person as if you don't already know what they'll say. Ask instead of concluding.
cells.core:
You're steady when a group's meaning is up in the air — you name what's fair, you keep the argument from turning cruel, you hold the space. The story you carry is that you're just getting along with people. The fairness holding this group together is work you're doing, and nobody has credited you for it, including you.
This isn't a skill you lack. It's older than the position you hold. Before you were judging anything, you were someone listening. Go back to that. Where meaning is being made, hear one person the way a student would — curious, not already certain. You'll find the one speaking is you; the calm was built, and it can be owned.
